name: Athens
summary: Athens has been lived in for over three thousand years — from a Bronze Age citadel on the Acropolis to the city that gave the world democracy, philosophy and drama in its 5th-century-BC golden age. The Parthenon crowned that height; Rome, Byzantium and the Ottomans followed, and a Venetian shell shattered the temple in 1687. Chosen as the capital of a newly independent Greece in 1834, when it was barely a town, Athens grew into a metropolis of over three million beneath the ancient rock.

events.title: Mycenaean Athens
events.body: A fortified palace crowns the Acropolis in the Bronze Age.

events.title: An Ionian refuge
events.body: Athens survives the Bronze Age collapse and grows as an Ionian centre.

events.title: Draco’s harsh laws
events.body: Draco gives Athens its first written — and famously severe — law code.

events.title: Solon’s reforms
events.body: Solon reforms debt and citizenship, laying the ground for democracy.

events.title: Peisistratus the tyrant
events.body: The tyrant Peisistratus beautifies Athens and promotes its great festivals.

events.title: Democracy is born
events.body: Cleisthenes establishes the world’s first democracy at Athens.

events.title: Marathon
events.body: Athenian hoplites defeat the invading Persians on the plain of Marathon.

events.title: Salamis and the sack
events.body: Persia burns the Acropolis, but the Athenian fleet wins a decisive victory at Salamis.

events.title: The Parthenon
events.body: Under Pericles the Parthenon rises on the rebuilt Acropolis at the height of Athens’ power.

events.title: The Peloponnesian War
events.body: Athens and Sparta begin a long war that will end the Athenian golden age.

events.title: The death of Socrates
events.body: Socrates is condemned by an Athenian jury and drinks hemlock.

events.title: Plato’s Academy
events.body: Plato founds the Academy; Aristotle’s Lyceum will follow.

events.title: Macedon takes Greece
events.body: Philip II of Macedon defeats Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea.

events.title: Rome sacks Athens
events.body: The Roman general Sulla storms and plunders the city.

events.title: Hadrian’s Athens
events.body: The emperor Hadrian lavishes new buildings and a great arch on the city.

events.title: The schools are closed
events.body: The emperor Justinian closes the ancient philosophical schools of Athens.

events.title: Frankish Athens
events.body: Crusaders seize Athens and the Parthenon becomes a Latin cathedral.

events.title: The Ottoman conquest
events.body: The Ottomans take Athens; the Parthenon is turned into a mosque.

events.title: The Parthenon explodes
events.body: A Venetian shell ignites Ottoman gunpowder stored in the Parthenon, wrecking the temple.

events.title: The Elgin Marbles
events.body: Lord Elgin removes much of the Parthenon’s sculpture to Britain.

events.title: Capital of Greece
events.body: After independence, Athens — then a small town — is chosen as capital of the new Greek kingdom.

events.title: The first modern Olympics
events.body: Athens hosts the revived Olympic Games.

events.title: The refugee flood
events.body: Nearly a million Greek refugees from Anatolia swell the city.

events.title: Occupation and civil war
events.body: Nazi occupation ends, but fighting in Athens opens the Greek Civil War.

events.title: Into Europe
events.body: Greece joins the European Community, with Athens as its capital.

events.title: The Games return
events.body: Athens hosts the Summer Olympics for the first time since 1896.

events.title: The debt crisis
events.body: A sovereign-debt crisis brings years of austerity and protest to the streets of Athens.

caveats: This timeline is compiled from general reference works — listed under Sources — rather than an event-by-event archive of primary documents, as the Mumbai timeline is. Treat it as a reliable outline, not a citation of record.
Dates for the earliest, legendary events are traditional rather than documented.
